title: Digital Read Serial
description: Wire a pushbutton with a pull-down resistor to digital pin 2, then read its state and print 0 or 1 to the Serial Monitor as you press and release the button.

steps.clip: Let's grab a pushbutton, a 10k ohm resistor, a few jumper wires, and your breadboard.
Straddle the pushbutton across the middle gap of the breadboard, so two legs land on each side.
hints: The button only fits one way across the gap — line its four legs up with two columns, two legs per column.
Press it in firmly so all four legs seat in their holes.

steps.clip: Run a wire from one of the button's legs to the 5V pin on the Arduino.
hints: Use either leg on the side of the button away from where pin 2 will connect.
This side of the button will supply 5 volts when it's pressed.

steps.clip: Now run a wire from the button's other leg to digital pin 2.
hints: This is the leg on the opposite side of the gap from the one you just wired.
Pin 2 will read HIGH or LOW depending on whether the button is pressed.

steps.clip: Push one leg of the resistor into the same column as the button's pin-2 leg.
hints: Use an empty row in that same column so the resistor's leg shares the strip with the button's leg.
This resistor pulls pin 2 LOW when the button isn't pressed.

steps.clip: Wire the resistor's other leg to GND on the Arduino.
hints: Any GND pin on the board works.
This finishes the pull-down path so pin 2 always reads a solid HIGH or LOW, never a floating value.

steps.clip: Upload the sketch and open the Serial Monitor to watch 0s and 1s as you press and release the button.
